passage_text: Researchers studied the effect of a novel antihypertensive agent, Hypotensol, on systolic blood pressure (SBP) in adults with stage 1 hypertension. A double‑blind, randomized, placebo‑controlled trial enrolled 200 participants (100 per arm). Baseline SBP was measured after a 5‑minute seated rest. Participants received either 10 mg Hypotensol daily or placebo for 4 weeks. SBP was reassessed at week 4 using the same protocol. The study aimed to determine whether Hypotensol could produce a clinically meaningful reduction in SBP compared to placebo. Secondary outcomes included changes in diastolic blood pressure (DBP) and incidence of adverse events. The investigators hypothesized a mean SBP reduction of at least 10 mmHg in the treatment group, with a standard deviation of 12 mmHg. Data were analyzed using an intention‑to‑treat approach, and significance was set at p < .05. The trial was conducted across three academic centers, and all participants provided written informed consent.
table_data:
Hypotensol arm (n = 100)
Baseline SBP (mmHg) | Mean ± SD | 140.5 ± 12.3
After 4 weeks SBP (mmHg) | Mean ± SD | 128.7 ± 11.8
Change in SBP (mmHg) | Mean ± SD | -11.8 ± 5.4
p‑value (change from baseline) | | < .001
Baseline DBP (mmHg) | Mean ± SD | 90.2 ± 8.7
After 4 weeks DBP (mmHg) | Mean ± SD | 88.5 ± 8.1
Change in DBP (mmHg) | Mean ± SD | -1.7 ± 3.9
p‑value (change from baseline) | | .12
stem: Which of the following best describes the primary outcome of the Hypotensol trial?

options.A: Reduction in diastolic blood pressure compared to placebo
options.B: Reduction in systolic blood pressure compared to placebo
options.C: Incidence of adverse events in the treatment group
options.D: Change in heart rate over the 4‑week period

explanation: Correct: B) The passage states the aim was a reduction in SBP compared with placebo; the table reports the SBP change (-11.8 mmHg) in the Hypotensol arm. Why the others are wrong: A) DBP and adverse events are described as secondary outcomes. C) Adverse events are secondary. D) Heart rate is not mentioned.
trap: Picking diastolic pressure because it appears in the table, though the passage names it a secondary outcome.
